Gavrilo Princip. A Bosnian-Serb nationalist whose assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand on June 28, 1914, precipitated the outbreak of World War I. At just nineteen years old, this member of the revolutionary group Black Hand fired the shots that shattered the fragile peace of Europe and triggered one of history's deadliest conflicts.

Princip was a nineteen-year-old member of the Black Hand, a Serbian nationalist organization dedicated to freeing Slavic territories from Austro-Hungarian rule. He suffered from tuberculosis and joined nationalist organizations partly to give his short life meaning and purpose before illness claimed him. He was part of a coordinated plot with six Serbian and Bosnian conspirators positioned along Franz Ferdinand's motorcade route in Sarajevo on June 28, 1914. The conspiracy involved Serbian military intelligence officers including Dragutin Dimitrijevic and the Black Hand, linking the assassination to state-level actors in Serbia.

Princip shot Archduke Franz Ferdinand and his wife Sophie during their motorcade in Sarajevo in Bosnia after an earlier bomb attack failed to kill the Archduke. Franz Ferdinand's visit to Sarajevo was intended as a show of Austro-Hungarian authority in newly annexed Bosnia-Herzegovina, which infuriated Serbian nationalists. Princip was originally equipped with a cyanide capsule intended for suicide after the assassination, consistent with Black Hand protocols for martyrdom. He fired at close range from the sidewalk, and both the Archduke and Sophie died shortly after being rushed to hospital.

Caught immediately after the shooting and tortured by Austro-Hungarian police, Princip saw Austria-Hungary blame Serbia for the conspiracy and issue a harsh ultimatum. Serbia's rejection triggered Austro-Hungarian mobilization and the chain of alliances leading to general war. Princip died in prison in 1918 from tuberculosis, becoming a martyr figure in Yugoslav nationalism, and his grave later became a pilgrimage site. His act demonstrated how nationalist zealotry and great-power entanglements could ignite global catastrophe.
